clusters.title: Apply the screen's visual resources
clusters.reasoning: These adjacent concepts are complementary parts of supplying a screen's appearance: shared Material styling and a declared bundled image. Both require only widget composition, already taught before this tile. Keep theme inheritance and asset declaration/loading as distinct sub-concepts, not interchangeable mechanisms. The inspector remains a separate diagnostic step.

clusters.title: Make a control identifiable and reachable
clusters.reasoning: These adjacent concepts address two complementary checks on the same accessible control: its accessible name and its interactive area. Widget composition and layout constraints are available at the tile's start; neither concept requires the earlier responsive-layout or text-scaling concepts in this tile. Preserve separate naming and target-size checks rather than imply that either alone establishes accessibility.

clusters.title: Present asynchronous results to a live UI owner
clusters.reasoning: These adjacent concepts are complementary parts of handling an asynchronous completion: choosing its presentation state and checking whether its UI owner can still receive an update. Their Dart asynchronous, conditional and class foundations, notifier updates, State lifecycle and local setState prerequisites are all earlier than this tile. Retain the boundary between what result state to publish and whether an owner is still mounted; request recovery and stale-result handling remain separate later concepts.

clusters.title: Select and resolve a compatible package
clusters.reasoning: These adjacent concepts form a package-adoption workflow: evaluate a candidate against feature and platform requirements, then resolve compatible dependency constraints reproducibly. Selection has no direct prerequisites and package imports precede this tile, so both can be entered at the tile's start. Preserve suitability evaluation versus version resolution as distinct checks; platform plugin configuration remains separate because it requires dependency compatibility taught within this tile.

clusters.title: Change and observe the sign-in session
clusters.reasoning: These adjacent concepts are the command and observation sides of one authentication workflow: await sign-in/sign-out operations and observe the session stream. FlutterFire initialization, async/await, stream subscriptions and notifier updates are all taught before this tile. Keep operation completion and stream-observed session state explicitly distinct; route access is excluded because it depends on session observation introduced here.

clusters.title: Identify the app and its release
clusters.reasoning: These adjacent concepts supply complementary release identifiers: which registered application the build belongs to and which version/build it represents. Both have no direct prerequisites and can be entered at this tile's start. Keep application identity distinct from release versioning, and preserve the Android and iOS rules within each concept rather than imply one universal numbering rule. The dated release-requirements check stays separate because it requires both concepts.

clusters.title: Prepare the store review package
clusters.reasoning: These three adjacent concepts are complementary preparation checks for one store review package: accurate listing materials, implementation-matched privacy disclosures, and a working release journey with reviewer access. Their release-requirements, analytics, permissions, security, integration-testing and authentication prerequisites all precede this tile. Preserve each checklist and its separate acceptance criteria; store submission remains a subsequent step because it requires these preparations.
